title: The Little Red Hen
author: Traditional
source: Public domain. Retold from the traditional tale.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time, a little red hen lived in a farmyard with a dog, a cat, and a duck. One morning, scratching in the dirt, she found some grains of wheat.

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "Who will help me plant this wheat?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All summer the wheat grew tall and golden. At last it was ready.

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "Who will help me cut the wheat?"

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "Who will help me carry the wheat to the mill to be ground into flour?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she did — all the way to the mill and back, with the sack of flour on her back.

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "Who will help me bake the bread?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she did. Soon the whole farmyard smelled of warm, fresh bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The little red hen set the beautiful golden loaf on the windowsill to cool. Up trotted the dog, the cat, and the duck, sniffing the air.

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "And who will help me EAT the bread?"

segments.speaker: hen
segments.text: "Oh no, you won't! I planted the wheat, I cut it, I carried it to the mill, and I baked the bread — all by myself. Now my chicks and I shall eat it — all by ourselves!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And that is just what they did, down to the very last delicious crumb.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The dog, the cat, and the duck watched with rumbling bellies, and they felt very sorry indeed. And the next time the little red hen found some grains of wheat and asked, "Who will help me?" — all three of them shouted, "I WILL!" And from that day on, everyone in the farmyard helped with the work, and everyone shared the warm, fresh bread.
